body: Most of India's Street View coverage is made with the low-quality 'shitcam', characterized by brownish colors and sometimes a large circular blur.
India's Generation 4 coverage uses a smallcam with a lower mount and a big circular blur that can be transparent.
A significant part of India also features Generation 3 trekker coverage amid mostly shitcam shots.
India drives on the left side of the road.
India has a wide variety of scripts used across regions, helpful for regional identification.
English is an official language widely visible on signage throughout India.
Indian license plates are mostly white; commercial vehicles have yellow plates, and electric vehicles use green plates.
India typically uses black and white striped signposts, also common in Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.
Most Indian utility poles are square concrete with trident tops though styles vary widely; wooden poles are rare.
Hindi is common in central and northern India, using the distinctive Devanagari script with top horizontal lines.
Marathi uses Devanagari with occasional unique letters like absent in Hindi.
Punjabi in northwest India uses a softer script with broken bars and distinct letters like , , and .
Gujarati script, found in Gujarat, resembles Hindi's but lacks the top horizontal line.
Bengali and Assamese use similar scripts; Bengali is identifiable by left-facing triangular letter shapes.
Assamese adds unique characters like and to the Bengali script.
Kannada features smooth curves, small circles, and squiggly tails on letters; similar to Telugu.
Telugu resembles Kannada but often has checkmark-like diacritics atop letters.
Tamil script combines curves, straight lines, and right angles, with some letters featuring dot diacritics.
Oriya script is curvy with wide semicircles on letters and diacritics resembling wide curves above characters.
Malayalam script, common in Kerala, consists of simple curvy letters often featuring upside-down U shapes.
Manipuri (Meitei) uses a script with many vertical lines and right angles.
Mizo, spoken in Mizoram, uses the Latin script and is the most common language besides English there.
Meghalaya mainly uses English language and signage.
Yellow tuk tuks with black roofs are common in Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
Concrete holey poles are unique to Gujarat and some Union Territories, rarely appearing elsewhere.
Andhra Pradesh and Telangana commonly have poles divided into two sections, similar to Brazil.
Metal mesh poles are common in Sikkim.
Metal holey poles are commonly seen in Kerala.
Thin grey metal poles appear throughout northeastern India and Himalayan regions, often in pairs.
Light green electricity counters with small windows are typical in Punjab, rarely seen in Haryana.
Window-shaped metal poletops occur in Punjab and Haryana.
Trident poletops with a central insulator mounted at the top are found in Karnataka and occasionally Haryana.
Metal trident poletops with small bars on top appear frequently in Manipur.
Upside down triangle poletops below the pole top are common in Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, and some Madhya Pradesh areas.
Madhya Pradesh poles often have a metal bar shaped like an upside-down 'A' slightly below the top.
Trapezoid-shaped connectors on poles are typical in Chhattisgarh and also appear in Meghalaya, Tripura, and Maharashtra.
West Bengal features poletops with two vertical bars forming a tall narrow rectangle.
West Bengal also has poletops with two crossbars, connected by thin vertical and diagonal supports.
Northeastern India features poles with mixed even and uneven poletops.
Meghalaya and Arunachal Pradesh have poles with two diagonal bars forming a '<' shape.
Assam, Meghalaya, and Mizoram commonly feature poles with two crossbars and insulators; more bars suggest Meghalaya or Mizoram.
Assam has trident poletops with the middle bar bent at 90°.
Poletops with a short crossbar above a longer crossbar are found in Goa.
Black and white stripes on poles and trees are common markings in Tamil Nadu.
Five or more thin black and yellow stripes on poles are typical in Delhi.
Four thick black and yellow stripes on poles are found in Bihar.
Trees with four red and white stripes near the base are found in Bihar and sometimes Jharkhand.
Small yellow pole stickers are common in Kerala, rarely found elsewhere.
Rounded roof tiles in central India are often disorganized and unevenly lined.
Southern Indian roofs are bright orange, flat with ridges, especially in Tamil Nadu.
West Bengal has flat roof tiles with small diamond-shaped protrusions.
Large corrugated metal hip roofs are found in West Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha.
Metal roofs with small triangular tops are common in Northeast India.
Houses made of square panels separated by thin beams are prevalent in Northeast India.
Thatched roofs and hay mounds are common on the east coast and northern plains, varying from fine hay to palm fans by region.
Gurdwaras, identifiable by white domes and ornate walls, are concentrated in Punjab, often marked by the Sikh Khanda symbol.
Goa and Kerala have many wealthy and modern homes.
Chir pines with smooth conical crowns and long needles are mainly found in Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, and western Arunachal Pradesh.
Khasi pines are common in Meghalaya and Manipur, featuring jagged, disorganized crowns.
Euphorbia neriifolia cacti are used as fences in Gujarat, western Maharashtra, and southern Rajasthan.
Palmyra palms look like lollipops with fan-shaped leaves and consistent-width trunks, common in southern and eastern India.
Areca palms have thin trunks and small crowns, found near the southwest coast, northeast, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
Date palms grow primarily in drier central Indian regions.
Oil palm plantations are mainly in Andhra Pradesh's panhandle near Telangana.
Tea plantations are found in the northeast and far south, often in flat areas in Assam and northeastern West Bengal.
Sugarcane grows mostly in northern Uttar Pradesh and southwestern India.
Cotton cultivation is common in western India, especially Gujarat and Maharashtra.
Canola mostly grows around Rajasthan.
The tallest mountains in India are in the Himalayas.
Ladakh and northern Himachal Pradesh feature extremely dry, vegetation-free Himalayan landscapes.
India's northern plains are fertile, flat, and extensively farmed.
Dark soil occurs mainly in Maharashtra and surrounding areas.
Red soil is found near the southern west coast, Chhattisgarh, and western Odisha.
Western Rajasthan is recognized by a dry landscape with sandy soil.
The Western Ghats mountains in Maharashtra have distinct ridgelines and plateaus, greener in the south.
Mizoram features lush green valleys and hills with many small peaks.
Large square-shaped cars are seen in specific Indian areas; similar cars with visible hoods exist in Odisha.
Square-pattern thin wooden fences are common in Northeast India.
Buddhist prayer flags are found in Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.
Andaman and Nicobar Islands have black pole stickers with digits and arrows.
Chandigarh is a planned industrial city with unique infrastructure like blue sector signs, yellow streetlight markings, and numeric street signs.
Orange and bright green buses commonly serve Delhi.
Ahmedabad and Surat feature separated middle lanes for buses, but these lanes are often used by other vehicles.
Black taxis with yellow roofs are found in Meghalaya and Mumbai.
Sikkim taxis often have a painted yellow hood or a small yellow circle.
Elevated railways exist in multiple Indian cities including Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Kochi, Kolkata, and Mumbai.
The Telangana-Karnataka border area features houses with roofs of thin grey bricks, also found in walls and stockyards.
White painted clay huts are common in northwest Bihar and northeast Uttar Pradesh.
Wooden huts with cross patterns can be found in central Bihar.
Japanese cedar trees have tall narrow crowns, mainly near Sikkim-West Bengal border and Meghalaya.
Himalayan cedar is seen from Harsil to Gangotri and around Shimla.
Bhutan white pine has downward hanging needles, found in Mechuka Valley and Arunachal Pradesh.
Doum palms with multiple branches are nearly exclusive to Diu territory.
The endangered Indian pitcher plant is exclusive to Khasi Hills, mostly near NH206 north of Umlārem.
Western Uttarakhand is barren due to logging and erosion, especially near Dehradun at the Himachal Pradesh border.
Mechuka Valley is the only Northeast India site with snowy mountains, brown grass, and Bhutan white pines.
Chaukhamba mountain massif near Ukhimath has three distinct snow-covered peaks.
South of Shillong features V-shaped eroded green valleys with flat ridges, differing from Mizoram's less smooth hills.
Gujarat has salt flats and coastal marshes with sparse grass and shallow water; western Rajasthan is sandy desert with shrubs.
Tamil Nadu's southern tip has large monolithic mountains like Magenthiragiri hills.
Southern Tamil Nadu features flat bushy landscapes with very red soil.
Road NH326 in Odisha west of Brahmapur has a grey antenna; images there are high quality for shitcam.
Parts of roads NH6 and NH206 near Shillong have yellow outer road lines, fresh dark pavement, and khasi pines.
